html:
Napoleon Bonaparte was a French general who rose during the French Revolution, seized power in 1799 and crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804. He conquered much of Europe before his final defeat in 1815, and left the Napoleonic Code, a model for civil law in many countries.

He was born in Corsica in 1769, a year after France bought the island from Genoa. The Revolution opened careers to talent, and he made his name as an artillery officer at Toulon in 1793, then won a run of victories in Italy in 1796 and 1797. A campaign in Egypt followed, the invasion of 1798. Back in Paris, he took power in the coup of 18 Brumaire in 1799 as First Consul.

At home he built a strong central state: the Civil Code, prefects running each department, the Bank of France, a peace with the Catholic Church and elite secondary schools.

Abroad, his wars remade the map:

  • Victories at Austerlitz (1805), Jena (1806) and Wagram (1809).
  • He ended the Holy Roman Empire and the Venetian Republic, and put his brothers on thrones.
  • He sold Louisiana to the United States in 1803.
  • Britain kept control of the sea after Trafalgar (1805), and he tried to choke its trade with a blockade.

The invasion of Russia in 1812 destroyed his army. Allied armies took Paris in 1814 and he was exiled to Elba. He returned for the Hundred Days in 1815, lost at Waterloo, and died on the island of Saint Helena in 1821. His campaigns spread French laws and the idea of the nation across Europe, and his invasion of Spain set off the independence wars of Spanish America.
